reason: The warm afternoon starts the heat-loss scenario and is the only available action.
expectation: The body will encounter warmth, likely setting up a sweating response.

effect: Warming is sensed by the skin and brain, setting up a response involving skin vessels.
reaction: The signal route is clear, though the result is close to what I expected.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should advance the heat-loss response.
expectation: The skin vessels may widen, bringing more blood near the surface to release heat.

effect: The wider skin arteriole brings more blood near the surface, supporting heat transfer toward the skin.
reaction: The control route and vessel change are clear, and matched my expectation.
reason: Adding sweat glands is the only offered combination and advances the evaporation goal.
expectation: The glands will produce sweat on the skin, setting up evaporation.

effect: Sweat reaches the skin, but the result makes clear that evaporation is needed to carry heat away.
reaction: The distinction between sweating and evaporation is useful and clear.
reason: Air at the skin is the only offered combination and should advance the evaporation goal.
expectation: Sweat will evaporate into the air and carry heat away from the body.

effect: Evaporation carries heat away, and the weaker sweat signal shows the response easing as core temperature returns toward its earlier range. The goal now shifts to cold.
reaction: The feedback shown by the fading signal is a useful detail.
reason: Cold evening is the only offered combination and starts the new goal.
expectation: The body will sense the colder surroundings and begin a response that conserves or produces heat.

effect: Cold is sensed by the skin and brain, and the sweat signal decreases; the vessel response is next.
reaction: The reduced sweating makes the transition to cold clear.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should advance the heat-conservation goal.
expectation: The skin vessels may narrow, reducing blood flow near the surface and heat loss.

effect: The narrowed skin vessels reduce heat transfer to the surface, but another response is needed to make heat.
reaction: The distinction between conserving and making heat is clear.
reason: Skeletal muscle is the only offered combination and should address heat production.
expectation: The muscles may shiver, producing heat through repeated contractions.

effect: Shivering adds heat through repeated muscle contractions that use ATP, complementing the reduced heat loss from narrowed skin vessels.
reaction: The link back to muscle work was satisfying and made the two cold responses distinct.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding skeletal muscle was most worthwhile: it connected shivering and ATP use to heat production, alongside the earlier conservation response.

leastWorthwhile.text: The initial warming step was straightforward but offered little decision-making; it was the only available action and mainly set up the sequence.

surprise.text: The fading sweat signal as core temperature moved toward its earlier range made the feedback aspect clearer than simply showing sweat evaporate.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless: the combinations followed a clear temperature-response sequence. However, every decision offered only one combination, so I did not discover the relationships by choosing between alternatives.

continue.text: I would be somewhat interested in another chapter for similarly clear connections between body systems, though the single-option sequence made the gameplay feel predictable.
